svg.text: A / B / C type trains, and what they demand of a station
Chinese metro classification. The car width sets the platform edge, the door count sets the boarding rate, the power pickup decides tunnel or viaduct.
SIDE ELEVATION (3 cars, 22.0 m each, consist repeats)
vmax 80 - 100 km/h doors 5 doors / side, 1.4 m
Over-ground lines usually run catenary, so the
platform needs no ceiling clearance and the
station can open to the sky.
catenary 1500 V DC or 25 kV AC (viaduct
SIDE ELEVATION (3 cars, 19.5 m each, consist repeats)
third rail at track level - collector shoe under the bogie
vmax 80 km/h doors 4 doors / side, 1.3 m
The workhorse of Chinese city metros. Third
rail forces a tunnel or a covered box, which
is exactly why B lines run behind platform
SIDE ELEVATION (3 cars, 19.0 m each, consist repeats)
third rail at track level - collector shoe under the bogie
vmax 80 km/h doors 4 doors / side, 1.2 m
Lighter profile for lower-demand branches and
automated lines. Narrower cars mean narrower
platforms and cheaper stations - but the crush
third rail 750 V DC / linear-motor var
05b ROLLING STOCK IS A CHOICE, NOT A DRAWING
Five decisions name and shape the train. Type and consist set capacity; power, colour and name identify the line.
the pickup decides tunnel or viaduct
one colour per line paints the car
the stock type no longer paints the car
A line is the unit you edit. Everything else - dwell, headway, boarding rate, where it can run - follows from these five.
05c PLATFORM SCREEN DOORS: FULL HEIGHT OR HALF HEIGHT
The same door cadence, two screens. Full height seals the platform; half height leaves the top open for smoke clearance and costs less.
sealed floor to soffit · paid-area air control
waist-high barrier · open above for smoke
crush load; rated is about 80% of crush. A train that cannot finish boarding leaves people behind - the core pressure readout.

Simulation contract: a line is {stock type, consist length, power, colour, name}. A train is {type, cars, doorsPerCar, doorWidth, dwellBase, maxLoad}. Boarding rate = f(doorWidth, crowding, alighting count). The PSD, full or half height, adds a fixed per-door transfer cost.
